_readme: FROZEN HELD-OUT SET. Do not tune against this file. Do not add a question because the brain
already answers it, and do not change an expectation because the brain disagrees — a failure
here is a finding, not a bug in the question.
Every expectation below was chosen from first principles ('which repo obviously owns this
capability?') BEFORE the brain was ever run against it. That is what makes it held-out. The
questions are phrased the way a newcomer would ask, deliberately avoiding the vocabulary of the
capability cards, so the retrieval has to actually work rather than string-match.
'concepts' is always allowed alongside the owning repo: it is the prose layer that summarizes
each repo, so a hit there is a correct answer to the same question.
Scored by scripts/eval-brain.mjs. The gate is GROUND TRUTH, never a model judge: a citation
must resolve to a passage that really exists on disk. An LLM panel once scored a zero-citation
answer 98/100 on this repo — model-as-judge is blind to the one failure that matters.

questions.query: I need to search a million embeddings on a laptop with no database server running.
questions.why: zero-server on-disk ANN search is ruvector/RVF's defining claim

questions.query: I want to try a risky change to an agent's memory and throw it away if it goes wrong.
questions.why: copy-on-write branch + rollback of a vector store is agenticow's whole purpose

questions.query: What can generate tests for my code and tell me which parts are untested?
questions.why: test generation and coverage analysis is agentic-qe's remit

questions.query: How do I spend less money on model calls without getting dumber answers?
questions.why: cost-optimized routing lives in agentic-flow; the cheap-then-escalate cascade is the harness's

questions.query: Is there a step-by-step method that takes me from a written spec to finished code?
questions.why: SPARC is the named specification-to-completion methodology

questions.query: I want to keep structured agent state and ask questions about how facts relate to each other.
questions.why: AgentDB owns structured agent memory incl. the causal/graph layer

questions.query: How do I make repeated vector lookups instant instead of recomputing them?
questions.why: RuLake is the read cache in front of vector stores

questions.query: Can I train a small neural network in Rust without dragging in Python?
questions.why: ruv-fann is the Rust neural network library

questions.query: I need messages between nodes to stay secure even against a future quantum computer.
questions.why: QuDAG is the quantum-resistant DAG communication layer

questions.query: How do I improve my agent's scaffolding without swapping out the model itself?
questions.why: 'freeze the model, evolve the harness' is metaharness / agent-harness-generator

questions.query: What coordinates several coding agents working at the same time on one task?
questions.why: Ruflo is the orchestration engine (swarms, agent spawn, task orchestration)

questions.query: How would I measure whether an AI actually fixed a real security vulnerability?
questions.why: cve-bench grades a patch against the project's own security regression test
